diagnosis.summary: Payment-service p95 latency has risen from 110 ms to 2,900 ms, a roughly 26x increase, and order-service is now returning 5xx errors on 16.7% of requests. Both services are severely degraded and have been in this state for 2 minutes.
diagnosis.root_cause: A sharp increase in payment-service response time, active concurrently with order-service call failures and elevated end-to-end latency, is the most likely root cause of this DEPENDENCY_FAILURE.
evidence: Payment-service p95 latency rose from 110 ms to 2,900 ms, a 26x increase over baseline.
Order-service p95 latency to the payment dependency rose from 112 ms to 2,950 ms, matching the payment-service degradation.
Order-service is recording 57 dependency errors per minute against a baseline of 0.
Order-service end-to-end p95 latency rose from 130 ms to 2,950 ms, a roughly 23x increase.
Order-service 5xx error rate is now 16.7%, up from 0.0% at baseline.

Payment-service p95 latency rose above its baseline at 14:32:00 and order-service 5xx errors rose above their baseline at 14:32:40, about 40 seconds later (observed sequence from correlated timestamps).
recommended_actions: Inspect payment-service Lambda logs and X-Ray traces starting at 14:32:00 for errors, timeouts, or unusual execution patterns.
Check payment-service Lambda concurrency and throttle metrics to determine whether invocations are being limited or queued.
Review payment-service cold start counts and mean handler duration to identify whether Lambda execution itself has slowed.
Consider adding or reducing the timeout on the order-service call to payment-service to fail fast and shed load while the root issue is investigated.
If payment-service cannot be stabilised quickly, evaluate circuit-breaking or temporarily disabling POST /orders to protect downstream customers from further 5xx responses.
